### cagrilintide-10 — Cagrilintide 10 mg
Summary

Cagrilintide is a long-acting acylated amylin analogue developed by Novo Nordisk for the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes. It mimics the pancreatic hormone amylin to reduce appetite, slow gastric emptying, and promote satiety. In clinical trials, it has been studied both as a monotherapy and in combination with semaglutide (as CagriSema), demonstrating meaningful and sustained body weight reduction.

Typical dose 0.3 mg/week escalating to up to 4.5 mg/week (clinical trial protocol); research vials dosed per investigator protocol

Half-life~7 days

Route Subcutaneous

Cycle length 16–32 weeks (per clinical trial protocols; long-term use under investigation)

Mechanism

## How it works

Cagrilintide binds to amylin receptors (AMY1R, AMY2R, AMY3R), which are heterodimers of the calcitonin receptor and receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMPs 1, 2, or 3), activating cAMP-mediated signaling pathways in the hypothalamus, area postrema, and nucleus of the solitary tract. This activation suppresses glucagon secretion, slows gastric emptying, and reduces food intake by enhancing central satiety signaling. The fatty acid acylation of cagrilintide extends its half-life to approximately 7 days, enabling once-weekly subcutaneous dosing.

Reported in research

## Benefits

*   Significant and sustained body weight reduction (up to ~10–15% in phase 2 trials as monotherapy; greater reductions in combination with semaglutide)
*   Reduction in caloric intake through centrally mediated appetite suppression and enhanced satiety
*   Slowing of gastric emptying, leading to improved postprandial glucose control
*   Suppression of inappropriate glucagon secretion, supporting glycemic regulation in type 2 diabetes

Context, not a prescription
